overview.text: The Red-lipped (Herald) Snake is a common, mildly venomous snake of Africa south of the Sahara. It is harmless to people.

identification.text: Olive-green or grey body with white speckles, a black head, and a red, yellow, white or black upper lip.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 70 cm long on average, up to 1 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Widespread in Africa south of the Sahara, from Senegal and Ethiopia to South Africa.

habitat.text: Marshy areas in lowland forest, moist savanna, grassland and fynbos.

diet.text: Amphibians, including rain frogs, and lizards.

reproduction.text: Lays 6 to 19 eggs in early summer.

recognise.text: Red (or yellow) upper lip and a dark head.
